newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to privatise all future highway projects.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to privatise all future highway projects.

text.p: Malaysia plans to privatise the building of all its future highways and expressways, the national Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.

It quoted Works Minister S. Samy Vellu as saying that more than 100 proposals for new road projects have been submitted by private companies to the Economic Planning Unit in Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's office.

Samy Vellu said the government has estimated road works to cost the country about 26 billion ringgit ($10.4 billion) until the year 2000 and that 17 billion ringgit or 65 percent of this would come from the private sector.
"That would mean the involvement of private companies in road construction will increase two or three fold," Samy Vellu said.
He said the government will maintain and upgrade existing roads and build the smaller ones.
Samy Vellu said the Malaysian road network has grown steadily from 16,400 km in 1970 to about 61,200 km now.
